main_body: Flat brick/stone paving pattern filling the whole tile area, with rows of light-topped stones separated by dark mortar lines
top_band: none. The column scan shows a repeating brick course pattern (dark mortar L=50, stone L=90 to 143, with a highlight row at 5, 21 and so on), not an object with a top and a front
evidence: This is a seamless terrain patch (paving or wall-face texture), not a standing object, so the top-band plus front-face contract does not apply. Each brick has a lighter top highlight with darker lower rows, which suits a ground or wall autotile. No receding side faces and no standing volume are drawn. Nothing in the drawing breaks the contract for terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours in total and a median of 5 per tile. The paving reference has 7, and the grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile. Beodeul tiles are information-rich at about 10 per tile, so this is clearly lower. 100% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the mortar and outline are a neutral dark-grey line with no material tint, which is the sticker look. The bricks repeat identically, with no per-stone variation, speckle or grain beyond one highlight row. There are no large flat fills, but the shading is shallow and uniform next to the references.
